'''Lisa Sauermann''' (born 25 September 1992) is a German mathematician known for her performance in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]], where in 2011 she had the single highest (and perfect) score. She won four gold medals (2008–2011) and one silver medal (2007) at the olympiad, representing Germany.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.imo-official.org/hall.aspx |title=Hall of Fame |publisher=International Mathematical Olympiad |accessdate=2013-05-20}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://official.imo2011.nl/year_individual_r.aspx?year=2011 |title=52nd IMO 2011: Individual results |publisher=International Mathematical Olympiad |accessdate=2013-05-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130307135922/http://official.imo2011.nl/year_individual_r.aspx?year=2011 |archive-date=2013-03-07 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Sauermann attended [[Martin-Andersen-Nexö-Gymnasium Dresden]] when she was in 12th grade. She won the Franz Ludwig Gehe Prize in 2011 and the gold medal in the age group III, the 11th–12th grade competition. As a result, she won a trip to the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences|Royal Academy of Sciences]] in Stockholm. To achieve this, she presented a new mathematical theorem with a proof in a work entitled "Forests with Hypergraphs".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.celesio.com/en/CR/Our_responsibility/Society/Education/Gehe-Prize2011/ |title=Franz Ludwig Gehe Prize 2011: forests with hypergraphs and smart satchels |publisher=Celesio |accessdate=2013-05-20 |archive-date=2015-07-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150719094652/http://www.celesio.com/en/CR/Our_responsibility/Society/Education/Gehe-Prize2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2011 she began studying mathematics at the [[University of Bonn]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Noack|first=Rick|title=Mein erstes Mal: Lisa, 18, wird Mathe-Weltmeisterin|url=http://www.spiegel.de/schulspiegel/leben/mein-erstes-mal-lisa-18-wird-mathe-weltmeisterin-a-786076.html|newspaper=Spiegel Online|date=5 October 2011}}</ref> In 2014, she completed her bachelor thesis on [[algebraic geometry]] under [[Michael Rapoport]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mullas |first1=Raffaella |title=A conversation with Lisa Sauermann |url=https://www.europeanwomeninmaths.org/lisa_sauermann/ |website=[[European Women in Mathematics]] |access-date=26 March 2023 |date=10 September 2022}}</ref> She became a graduate student studying with [[Jacob Fox]] at [[Stanford University]] where she obtained her PhD in 2019, receiving two prizes for her dissertation titled "Modern Methods in Extremal Combinatorics".<ref>{{Cite web|date=September 8, 2020|title=Lisa Sauermann Receives Two Dissertation Prizes|url=https://mathematics.stanford.edu/news/lisa-sauermann-receives-two-dissertation-prizes|access-date=2021-11-24|website=mathematics.stanford.edu|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sauermann |first=Lisa |date=May 2019 |title=Modern Methods in Extremal Combinatorics |url=https://purl.stanford.edu/jk244dk0869 |access-date=1 October 2023}}</ref> After her graduation she worked as an assistant professor at Stanford before spending a year at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton]]. In 2021 became an assistant professor at [[MIT]] and received the [[European Prize in Combinatorics]] at [[Eurocomb]] for her work in combinatorics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lisa Sauermann Awarded European Prize in Combinatorics – Women In Math |url=https://math.mit.edu/wim/2021/11/23/lisa-sauermann-awarded-european-prize-in-combinatorics/ |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=math.mit.edu}}</ref> In 2023 she accepted a tenured professorship at [[University of Bonn]], where she currently works,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.uni-bonn.de/en/news/sauermann | title=Lisa Sauermann Returns to the University of Bonn }}</ref> her main field of work {{as of|2023|lc=yes}} being [[probabilistic combinatorics]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://idw-online.de/de/news820314 |title=Lisa Sauermann erhält einen renommierten Hausdorff Chair am Exzellenzcluster HCM |trans-title=Lisa Sauermann receives a renowned Hausdorff Chair at the HCM Excellence Cluster |first=Johannes |last=Seiler |work=[[Informationsdienst Wissenschaft|idw]] |date=8 September 2023 |access-date=18 April 2025 }}</ref> In 2022, she was awarded a [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan fellowship]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 Fellows {{!}} Alfred P. Sloan Foundation |url=https://sloan.org/fellowships/2022-Fellows |access-date=2022-09-25 |website=sloan.org }}</ref> and in 2023, she received the von Kaven Award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lisa Sauermann receives the von Kaven Award |url=https://www.uni-bonn.de/en/news/205-2023 |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=Universität Bonn |language=en}}</ref>

Her sister, Anne, two years her junior, was a successful participant in math and science Olympiads at the national level.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.manos-dresden.de/schule/erfolge.php?jahr=1112 |title=Martin-Andersen-Nexö-Gymnasium Dresden |publisher=Manos-dresden.de |date= |accessdate=2015-06-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150610085917/http://www.manos-dresden.de/schule/erfolge.php?jahr=1112 |archive-date=2015-06-10 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
